defects: Integrability hypothesis is strengthened: uses `Integrable f` (integrable on all of ℝ) instead of gold's `IntegrableOn f (Ioi 0)` (integrable only on (0,∞)), excluding valid functions that are integrable on (0,∞) but not on all of ℝ

Non-negativity hypothesis is strengthened: requires `0 ≤ f x` for all `x ≥ 0` (including x=0) instead of gold's `∀ t ∈ Ioi 0, 0 ≤ f t` (only requires non-negativity on (0,∞)), excluding valid cases where f(0) < 0 but the conclusion still holds
